• Define and own the roadmap, prioritizing opportunities across billing, claims, collections, and pre-billing workflows where AI can reduce denials, surface missed revenue, and reduce manual effort.

PGCE Teaching Practice Assessors play a vital role in ensuring the academic quality, fairness, and integrity of student assessment within school-based teaching practice. Successful applicants will contribute to the assessment of teaching practice evidence aligned with South African higher education standards and institutional quality assurance requirements.

Specialisation Area

• Teaching Practice and Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)

• Teaching Practice Portfolios and Reflective Practice

·School-Based Practicum Assessment

• Evaluate student submissions to ensure assessment decisions are valid, reliable, fair, consistent, and academically rigorous.

• Provide constructive academic feedback to students in accordance with approved rubrics and assessment guidelines.

• Understanding of curriculum, assessment practices, and Work-Integrated Learning in higher education.

• Knowledge of South African education contexts and school-based teaching practice frameworks.

• Strong attention to detail and quality assurance principles.

• Ability to work independently and meet strict assessment deadlines.

• Good communication and collaboration skills.

• Proficiency in digital platforms and online learning environments.

Minimum Requirements

• A master’s degree in Education, Teacher Education, Curriculum Studies, or a related specialisation (essential).

• At least two years’ experience in higher education, teacher education, Teaching Practice, assessment, curriculum design, or academic reviewing.

• Demonstrable experience assessing, marking, moderating, or reviewing academic work or Teaching Practice evidence.

• Experience in distance or online education will serve as an advantage.

• Familiarity with South African higher education quality assurance frameworks.

• Computer literacy with access to a reliable internet connection and laptop/desktop.

Added Advantage
​

• A Doctorate in the relevant field or progress towards one.

• Experience within private higher education institutions.

• Previous experience in distance learning institutions or Teaching Practice assessment.

Application Process Interested applicants are invited to submit:

• A comprehensive CV detailing academic and professional experience.

title: Accounting Automation Engineer
description:
Spotter Labs is hiring Accounting Automation Engineers to help automate manual processes across accounting, finance, and related business systems.
This role is for someone who can understand how work is being done today, identify repetitive manual steps, connect data across systems, build automation, and create cleaner workflows that are accurate, repeatable, and scalable.
The initial focus will be Accounting and Finance, but strong performers may also support automation projects in other departments as the company continues to grow.
What You Will Do

• Review manual accounting and finance workflows and identify opportunities for automation.

• Build repeatable processes across multiple systems, exports, reports, and data sources.

• Improve reconciliations, journal-entry preparation, close tracking, reporting, and exception management.

• Help connect operational data to accounting and finance processes.

• Create templates, scripts, dashboards, workflows, and documentation that reduce manual work.

• Work with accounting, finance, operations, and technology teams to understand process gaps and build practical solutions.

• Design controls so automation improves accuracy rather than simply speeding up bad processes.

• Create exception-based workflows so teams can focus on issues instead of routine data entry.

• Document processes clearly so they can be maintained and improved over time.

What We Are Looking For
We are looking for practical automation builders who can work across business systems and messy real-world data.
The ideal candidate has:

• Experience automating manual processes using tools such as Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Python, Power Query, VBA, Google Apps Script, Zapier, Make, Power Automate, APIs, or similar platforms.

• Strong ability to work with data exports, reports, spreadsheets, and system-generated files.

• Understanding of accounting or finance processes, including reconciliations, journal entries, month-end close, AP, payroll, reporting, or financial analysis.

• Ability to map a current process, identify failure points, and build a cleaner workflow.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to work with non-technical users and translate business problems into automated solutions.

• Good documentation habits.

• Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where systems and processes are still being built.

Preferred Experience

• Experience working with accounting, ERP, banking, payroll, expense management, inventory, reporting, or operational systems.

• Experience building dashboards, exception reports, reconciliation tools, or workflow automations.

• Experience with multi-system data matching and process improvement.

• Experience supporting accounting, finance, operations, logistics, transportation, or other data-heavy business environments.

• Accounting, finance, data analytics, systems, or engineering background preferred.

The Type of Person Who Will Succeed
This role is best for someone who likes solving practical business problems.
You should be able to look at a manual process and ask:

• Why is this being done manually?

• What data is needed?

• Where does the data come from?

• What can be automated safely?

• What should remain subject to review?

• How do we prove the output is accurate?

• How do we make the process repeatable?

We do not need someone who only writes code in isolation. We need someone who can understand the business process, work with the people doing the work, and build useful automation that holds up in the real world.
Hiring Process
Candidates may be asked to complete a practical work sample involving process mapping, data cleanup, reconciliation logic, automation design, reporting, or workflow improvement.
We are looking for candidates who can understand a problem, organize the data, build a practical solution, document their work, and explain how the process could be improved or automated.

title: Head of Compliance: Multilateral Trading Facility (MTF)
description:
Reports to: Regional Head of Compliance, EMEA (with matrix reporting to the OEM Board and Global Compliance) 

Regulator: Malta Financial Services Authority (MFSA) 

About the Team

The compliance function at OKX is responsible for the overall compliance culture at the company. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on the company's AML and regulatory obligations and enterprise risks.

OKX Europe Markets Limited is our MFSA-authorised investment services entity. Its licence covers the operation of a multilateral trading facility alongside our MiFID derivatives business. Operating a trading venue puts a distinct set of obligations on the firm: venue rulebook governance, member admission, market surveillance, transparency and reporting, systems resilience and orderly trading controls. This role owns compliance for that venue.

What You Will Be Doing

As Head of Compliance for the MTF, you will hold the MiFID compliance function for the trading venue and act as the MFSA-approved person for that role. The MLRO function sits separately; you will work alongside the OEM MLRO on financial crime matters that touch venue activity.

You will:

• Own the MTF compliance framework end to end: policies, procedures, controls, registers and the compliance monitoring programme covering MiFID II, MiFIR, MAR and the MFSA Investment Services Rules applicable to MTF operators.

• Act as the primary compliance point of contact for the MFSA on venue matters: authorisation variations, notifications, thematic reviews, RFIs, inspections and remediation.

• Own the venue rulebook. Keep it current, ensure it is enforceable, and run the governance process for changes.

• Oversee member and participant admission: eligibility criteria, non-discriminatory access, direct electronic access arrangements, sponsored access controls, and ongoing monitoring of members' compliance with the rules of the venue.

• Oversee admission to trading of financial instruments, including the compliance assessment of new instruments, product classes and tokenised or DLT-based instruments where relevant.

• Provide compliance oversight of orderly trading requirements: systems capacity and resilience, testing of members' algorithms, circuit breakers, order-to-trade ratios, tick sizes, market making schemes and clock synchronisation.

• Provide compliance oversight of pre- and post-trade transparency, waivers and deferrals, transaction reporting, reference data and the accuracy and completeness controls behind them.

• Advise the business on the interaction between the MTF and OKX's wider European footprint: the MiFID derivatives business, MiCA-authorised activity in OKX Europe Ltd, and the DLT Pilot Regime where a DLT MTF is in scope.

• Deliver the annual compliance risk assessment, the compliance monitoring plan and the compliance report to senior management and the Board.

• Build, lead and develop the MTF compliance team, and set the compliance training curriculum for venue-facing staff, trading operations and technology.

• Give day-to-day advice to product, engineering, trading operations, legal and market operations in a fast-moving regulatory environment, including sign-off on venue changes, launches and marketing where required.

• Oversee compliance aspects of outsourcing, critical third parties and operational resilience, including DORA obligations relevant to the venue.

• Prepare Board, committee and matrix stakeholder reporting, and represent OKX with the MFSA, ESMA consultations, industry bodies and peer venue forums.

What We Look For in You

• 10 years plus in regulatory compliance within financial services, market infrastructure, fintech or crypto, including time at a senior or head-of-function level.

• Direct experience of trading venue compliance: MTF, OTF, regulated market, SI or an equivalent execution venue. This is the core requirement.

• Working knowledge of MiFID II and MiFIR as they apply to venue operators: Artic

Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. - Own Mercor's identity infrastructure - Okta configuration and provisioning - managed as code in Terraform rather than clicked through a console

- Design and implement SCIM integrations across our SaaS stack, automating user provisioning and deprovisioning

- Own identity planning and architecture as we scale: access models, group strategy, and how entitlements evolve from hundreds to thousands of employees

- Own cloud account structure, IAM roles, and permission boundaries across AWS, GCP, Azure, and Vercel, keeping access least-privilege as the org grows

- Build and maintain Terraform for internal platforms so environments are reproducible and every change is reviewable

- Build automation that cuts manual ticket volume for employee onboarding and offboarding

- Design and own secrets management, key rotation, and service-account lifecycle

- Troubleshoot identity and infrastructure issues, trace root causes, and implement systemic fixes

- Document platform architecture, runbooks, and automation so the team can operate and extend it

- Mentor future IT team members on infrastructure-as-code, automation practices, and systems thinking

- Help establish sustainable escalation procedures as the team grows

You may be a good fit if you have:

Our client is a fast-growing SEO technology company that helps businesses acquire high-quality backlinks through a scalable and data-driven platform. By combining advanced automation, real-time tracking, and access to a large network of verified publishers, they enable SEO teams to execute link acquisition strategies more efficiently and at scale.
We are currently looking for an experienced Link Acquisition Specialist to join their remote team.
About the Role
As a Link Acquisition Specialist, you will play a key role in developing and executing backlink acquisition strategies for clients across a variety of industries. You will be responsible for identifying high-value link opportunities, evaluating publisher quality, monitoring campaign performance, and ensuring that acquired links contribute to measurable SEO growth.
This is a role for someone who understands that successful link acquisition is about far more than volume. You have a strong understanding of relevance, authority, risk assessment, and long-term SEO value, and you are comfortable making decisions based on data rather than assumptions.
You will work closely with internal stakeholders to align link acquisition efforts with broader SEO and marketing objectives while continuously identifying opportunities to improve campaign performance and return on investment.
Key Responsibilities

• Research, evaluate, and secure high-quality backlink opportunities

• Assess domain quality, topical relevance, authority metrics, and traffic potential

• Conduct competitor and market analysis to identify acquisition opportunities

• Develop and refine link acquisition strategies based on client objectives

• Monitor backlink performance and contribute recommendations for optimization

• Ensure timely activation, indexation, and quality control of acquired links

• Maintain accurate documentation and campaign reporting

• Collaborate with internal teams to align link-building activities with overall SEO strategy

• Build and maintain relationships with publishers and external partners where required

• Stay up to date with SEO trends, search engine developments, and industry best practices

• Report & collaborate directly with the CEO

Requirements
What You'll Bring
Previous experience working with link building and/or link acquisition is a must.

• Great understanding of backlink quality signals and SEO performance metrics

• Experience using SEO tools such as Ahrefs, Semrush, Majestic, or similar platforms

• Ability to evaluate domains based on metrics such as DR, DA, traffic, relevance, and link profile quality

• Strong outreach skills, in particular via e-mail & text outreach channels

• Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

• Professional communication skills, both written and verbal

• Comfortable working independently in a fully remote environment

• Experience from an SEO agency, affiliate marketing, iGaming, SaaS, or digital marketing environment, as well as experience with business negotiation, is considered highly advantageous

Benefits
Benefits

• Flexibility in a fully remote work setup

• Very competitive salary; 30-45k EUR base salary, depending on experience

• Commission based on performance & targets

• Work in a startup culture with ability to shape & improve procedures

• Build and expand your own portfolio of publication sites & link building partners with free hands

title: PeopleSoft Integration Developer
description:
Peoplesoft Integration Developer - Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Peoplesoft Integration Developer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000-$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 12+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary:
We are seeking an experienced PeopleSoft Integration Developer to design, build, and operate enterprise integrations connecting PeopleSoft applications to internal systems, cloud applications, and third-party platforms. This role focuses specifically on the integration layer, including service operations, queues, routings, transformations, security configurations, and error handling. The ideal candidate will combine deep hands-on Integration Broker experience with broader PeopleTools knowledge and a strong understanding of API and integration design patterns. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners - product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders - to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production.

Key Responsibilities

• Design and develop integration scenarios using PeopleSoft Integration Broker, including service operations, queues, routings, and handlers.

• Build synchronous and asynchronous integrations using REST and SOAP web services.

• Develop transformations using XSLT, Application Engine, and PeopleCode handlers, applying disciplined engineering practices and partnering closely with stakeholders to ensure outcomes are durable, well-documented, and aligned with broader team and platform standards.

• Configure security on inbound and outbound services, including WS-Security, OAuth2, and certificate-based authentication.

• Build robust error-handling and retry mechanisms, including notifications, monitoring, and resubmission workflows.

• Develop Component Interfaces and File Layouts to support hybrid integration scenarios.

• Lead migration efforts to retire legacy point-to-point integrations to standardized Integration Broker patterns, planning phased cutovers, building backward-compatibility shims where needed, and ensuring each migration step is reversible and well-monitored.

• Optimize performance of high-volume integrations through queue tuning, parallel processing, and asynchronous design.

• Integrate PeopleSoft with cloud applications (Oracle Cloud, Workday, ServiceNow) and middleware (OIC, MuleSoft, Boomi).

• Maintain comprehensive, current technical documentation - including architecture diagrams, design decisions, configuration references, runbooks, and operational procedures - so that the system remains supportable, auditable, and easy to onboard new engineers onto over time.

• Provide hypercare and post-go-live support, including incident response and root-cause analysis.

• Collaborate closely with functional consultants and integration architects, gathering requirements, aligning on technical approach, and ensuring that delivered solutions meet both functional needs and broader engineering and operational standards.

• Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers through code review, design review, pair programming, and structured knowledge sharing, helping the broader team grow in technical maturity and confidence over time.

Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

The AI Platform & Agentic Apps team builds the agent platform behind every AI agent at Robinhood. Today it gives a growing number of engineers and employees an AI teammate that ships code, queries data, and runs operational workflows on their behalf. We're building toward the same platform powering the agents millions of customers interact with directly, in real time. These agents don't just answer questions - they're designed to take real action across carefully curated meta harnesses. This is agentic AI at real scale, in a regulated financial environment, and it will change how Robinhood works!

As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer on the AI Platform & Agentic Apps team, you will design and build the harness that every agent at Robinhood runs on. A critical part of the role is making those agents trustworthy at scale: trajectory-level evals that measure how an agent reasons and acts, and action guardrails - permission models, approval gates, and sandboxing - built as platform primitives that other teams adopt. You'll be a technical anchor on a growing, high-caliber team, collaborating with product, infrastructure, and fellow ML engineers to take ambitious ideas from zero to one and into production. You'll help define the team's technical direction, mentor engineers, and shape how Robinhood decides an agent is ready to ship. This role offers a rare combination of technical depth, platform-scale impact, and the satisfaction of building systems that genuinely don't exist anywhere else.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

• Design and build the core of Robinhood's agent harness - orchestration, tool integrations, context and memory management - so one platform can safely power both high-trust internal agents and tightly scoped customer-facing ones.

• Ship agentic applications end to end on that harness, from an ambiguous problem to a production agent that takes real action on behalf of employees or customers, and feed what you learn back into the platform.

• Build trajectory-level evaluation systems that score how an agent got to an answer, not just the answer - tool-call correctness, planning and recovery, multi-step task completion - backed by simulation environments and synthetic task generation.

• Architect action guardrails as platform primitives: least-privilege tool scoping, permission models, human-approval gates for high-risk or irreversible actions, step and budget limits, sandboxing, and rollback.

• Make evals and guardrails products other teams adopt - SDKs, CI regression gates on prompt, model, and tool changes, continuous red-teaming, and production tracing that closes the loop from real traffic back into eval sets and guardrail models.

title: Mecánico de Motocicletas

Summary

El mecánico de motocicletas se especializa en inspeccionar, reparar y mantener motocicletas y otros vehículos de deportes motorizados. El rol implica realizar diagnósticos, reparar motores, afinar y abordar problemas eléctricos para asegurar que los vehículos estén en condiciones óptimas de funcionamiento. El mecánico debe cumplir con los protocolos de seguridad y garantizar que cada vehículo cumpla con los estándares regulatorios. Además, el mecánico brindará soporte a los clientes tanto en persona como a través de consultas remotas o virtuales, asesorando sobre reparaciones o mantenimiento necesarios, asegurando que los vehículos funcionen de acuerdo con las especificaciones del fabricante y manteniendo documentación detallada del servicio para apoyar tanto las interacciones en el taller como las virtuales. Los candidatos deben tener un teléfono inteligente moderno con una conexión a internet activa para gestionar eficientemente los pedidos y asignaciones a través de la aplicación de la empresa. La habilidad para navegar aplicaciones móviles, plataformas digitales y flujos de trabajo basados en aplicaciones es esencial para una ejecución fluida de tareas y comunicación.

La compensación varía entre $41,600 y $72,800 por año, según la experiencia y la disponibilidad.

Job Specifics

• Inspeccionar y diagnosticar problemas mecánicos y eléctricos en motocicletas y vehículos de deportes motorizados.

• Reparar y reemplazar motores, transmisiones, frenos, sistemas de suspensión y otros componentes mecánicos.

• Afinar motores para un rendimiento óptimo y abordar cualquier fallo eléctrico.

• Seguir procedimientos y pautas de seguridad durante las reparaciones para garantizar un servicio seguro y efectivo.

• Mantener el cumplimiento de las normativas y estándares de la industria en todos los trabajos de reparación.

• Mantener registros detallados de reparaciones, piezas utilizadas e historial de servicio del vehículo para futuras referencias.

• Brindar un excelente servicio al cliente, respondiendo preguntas sobre reparaciones y ofreciendo consejos sobre mantenimiento.

Qualifications and Experience

Qualifications

• Se requiere diploma de secundaria o GED. Experiencia:

• Al menos 2 años de experiencia trabajando como mecánico de motocicletas o en un campo relacionado con experiencia en reparación de motores pequeños.

Experience

• Certificación de mecánico de motocicletas (por ejemplo, de un programa acreditado).

• Más de 5 años de experiencia en mecánica de motocicletas, con habilidades avanzadas en solución de problemas.

• Familiaridad con software de diagnóstico para ayudar en la identificación de problemas complejos.

• Gran atención al detalle y compromiso con la realización de reparaciones de alta calidad.

Our innovative approach to remote mechanic jobs is reshaping the industry, offering unparalleled opportunities for skilled professionals like you. By joining our team, you'll be at the forefront of this revolution, leveraging cutting-edge technology to provide expert services from anywhere. With flexible schedules and the ability to work remotely, you'll enjoy greater freedom and autonomy in your career. Plus, our commitment to inclusivity ensures that every team member is valued and supported. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

title: Senior Product Policy Lead, Regulation

About the Team

The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment.

About the Role

As Product Policy Manager, Regulation, you will map external regulatory and legislative trends and synthesize them into concrete research, product, and policy requirements. You will connect deep expertise in regulation and public policy with a sophisticated understanding of AI and strong product judgment. Your remit will span frontier AI, youth, wellbeing, use in high-stakes domains, deceptive use, and other emerging issues. Working closely with Legal and Global Affairs, you will help Product, Engineering, Research, and Safety teams understand what external developments mean for their work, what decisions or evidence are needed, and how to act.

We’re looking for someone who combines deep regulatory and public-policy expertise with an in-depth understanding of AI and a demonstrated ability to advise product and engineering teams. You should be able to move from complex external developments to clear decisions and requirements that teams can implement.

This role can be based in San Francisco or remote. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

- Map and prioritize regulatory and legislative developments across jurisdictions and AI issue areas. Distinguish enacted requirements, proposals, guidance, and emerging expectations; assess their relevance, uncertainty, timing, and implications for our models and products.

- Translate external developments into actionable research questions, evaluation needs, product requirements, and policy recommendations. Identify gaps in evidence, define the intended outcome and acceptance criteria, and make tradeoffs and open questions clear.

- Advise Product, Engineering, Research, and Safety teams throughout design, launch, and iteration. Partner with Legal on legal interpretation and applicability, and with Global Affairs on legislative context and external engagement, to develop feasible implementation options and clear ownership.

- Maintain traceability from external signals to internal decisions, requirements, and implementation. Track material changes, surface dependencies and emerging risks, and use research, product evidence, and expert input to refine recommendations and inform external policy discussions.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Bring substantial experience in AI or technology regulation, public policy, product policy, or a related field, including interpreting complex regulatory and legislative developments across jurisdictions and translating them into action.

- Understand AI deeply, including model capabilities and limitations, training and deployment, evaluations, and safety mitigations. You can reason about how requirements differ at the model, product, and deployment levels and identify where further research is needed.

- Have a strong record of product advising and close partnership with product managers, engineers, and researchers. You can turn ambiguous concerns into specifications, implementation options, acceptance criteria, and decisions that improve products.

- Exercise sound judgment under uncertainty, prioritize across a broad portfolio, and manage work from an emerging external signal through implementation and iteration.

- Communicate clearly and precisely with technical teams, legal and policy experts, and executives. You can explain regulatory complexity, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and resolve disagreement constructively.

- Bring breadth across AI policy issues-including frontier risks, youth, wellbeing, high-stakes uses, and deceptive use-and the ability to build depth quickly with subject-matter experts, research, data

description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's RL Scaling Science team studies how reinforcement learning behaves as we scale it (across model size, compute, and task horizon) and turns that understanding into the training recipes behind our frontier models. As a Research Engineer on this team, you'll design and run large-scale experiments to understand and resolve bottlenecks, build the benchmarks that make long-horizon progress measurable, and ship validated findings directly into production training.

This role lives at the boundary between research and engineering. The problems are open, the experiments run at frontier scale, and the path from a robust result to production is short.

Key responsibilities

• Design, run, and interpret large-scale RL experiments, reasoning rigorously about what the data does and doesn't show

• Investigate how RL improves as horizon, compute, and model size grow

• Build and maintain benchmarks for long-horizon RL so progress is measurable and reproducible

• Translate validated findings into production training recipes, exercising judgment about when a result is robust enough to ship

• Debug complex issues at the seam where research meets infrastructure - failures that only appear at scale

Your Impact

As a Senior Search Engineer on our Discovery Team , you will build the retrieval layer behind product discovery for some of the world’s most demanding commerce brands.

Search is changing shape. Shoppers type full sentences instead of keywords, and increasingly the client calling our API is an AI agent rather than a person. We are on the path to take our semantic and hybrid retrieval to general availability, and tackling the hard problems: making it fast, affordable, measurably better across enterprise catalogs, and working out what comes after it. This role is hybrid, with three days a week spent in our Munich, Berlin, London or Valencia office.

You're a creative problem-solver who is wired to find solutions. You confidently dive into complex challenges and have a talent for making them simple for others. Your curiosity drives you to constantly grow and contribute to an environment of trust and teamwork.

Great ideas come from many paths, and your unique perspective matters more than checking every box. What matters most is the mindset you bring to the work.

• Experience with building search solutions on top of engines, such as Elasticsearch (preferred), Solr, OpenSearch, or similar.

• Aspiration to constantly improve yourself and learn new technologies, concepts, etc.

• Fluent English communication skills to work in international teams.

• AI Aptitude : A genuine curiosity for using AI tools to work smarter and more effectively, paired with a drive to learn and put them into practice in your role.

Nice to Have:

• Experience developing REST APIs and knowledge of scalable event-driven architectures (incl., queues, notification topics, sharding, replication, load balancing, and failover).

• Experience working with Scala or other functional programming languages.

• Experience with infrastructure work and other technologies like Helm, Kubernetes, and Rust.

Benefits

title: Microsoft Infrastructure Support Engineer
description:
The primary purpose of this position is to provide Microsoft core infrastructure support for Managed Services customers, with a strong focus on on-premises technologies including Windows Server, Active Directory, domain controllers, Group Policy, SCCM, and related Microsoft infrastructure. Cloud experience is valuable as a secondary skill set but is not the primary focus of this role. This role operates in a reactive break/fix support model. The Engineer works directly with multiple customers in a fast-paced, case-based environment to assess issues, troubleshoot root causes, drive cases to resolution, and deliver a high-quality customer experience. The position may be based anywhere in the United States, with working hours coordinated to support customer and team needs.
What You Will Do:

• Serve as a trusted technical support resource for customers experiencing Microsoft core infrastructure issues.

• Troubleshoot, diagnose, and resolve issues involving Windows Server, Active Directory, domain controllers, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, SCCM, endpoint management, and related Microsoft technologies.

• Support hybrid or cloud technologies, including Azure and Microsoft 365, when needed and aligned with the Engineer’s skill set.

• Assess customer issues quickly, identify root causes, and drive assigned cases through resolution.

• Manage service requests through a case queue, review assignments daily, and provide accurate and timely status updates.

• Document troubleshooting steps, resolutions, customer communications, incident details, and change activity in the appropriate tracking systems.

• Communicate technical problems, business impact, next steps, and solutions clearly and professionally to customers and stakeholders.

• Work directly with multiple customers each day and build trust through responsiveness, technical knowledge, and professional communication.

• Collaborate with peers and cross-functional teams to resolve complex technical issues and share knowledge.

• Engage Microsoft support or other technical resources when additional product expertise or escalation assistance is required.

• Understand service-level agreements in a production environment and work to meet customer commitments.

• Participate in an on-call rotation supporting critical systems.

• Participate in customer calls and work with account management personnel in support of the client relationship.

• Contribute to technical documentation, procedures, knowledge articles, templates, proposals, and training materials.

• Participate in client projects and infrastructure improvements as assigned.

• Mentor and support peers within the team and across CDW .

• Attend training and obtain industry-related certifications as determined by management.

• Manage multiple priorities, follow through on commitments, and complete tasks and projects on time.

• Communicate unanticipated events, risks, schedule changes, or technical concerns to the Engineering Manager.

• Identify potential customer needs or cross-selling opportunities and communicate them to the appropriate sales or account team.

• Adhere to time-entry, compliance, policy, and procedural requirements.

What We Expect of You:

• Bachelor's degree and 3 years of Microsoft support experience, or 7 years of total IT engineering experience, including 3 years of Microsoft support experience.

• Hands-on experience supporting Microsoft core infrastructure technologies, including Windows Server, Active Directory, domain controllers, and Group Policy.

• Depth of experience troubleshooting Windows Server, Active Directory, domain controllers, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, or SCCM in complex customer environments.

• Experience working in a ticket-driven, case-based, or reactive break/fix support environment.

• Customer-facing support experience with the ability to communicate professionally and clearly with multiple customers each day.

title: Donor Officer
description:
To support our mission and operational structure, we are only able to hire team members who are already authorized to work in the Unites States. Candidates MUST have existing legal work authorization, as visa sponsorship is not available.
We are looking for someone located in the Central or Eastern parts of the US.
About Our Mission
Greater Europe Mission is a community of disciple-makers that longs to see Europe transformed by Jesus. For over 70 years, our workers have created relationships and environments of grace where people who are near or far from God feel welcome.
On a continent where less than 3% of the population claim a relationship with Jesus, the light of the gospel is spreading! As more and more Europeans are awakened to hope in Jesus, the need for effective, reproducible discipleship is at an all time high.
Our US-based team works to connect the people of God in the US to the mission of God in Europe through recruiting, creating church partnerships, and raising funds to support the ministry.
Position Summary: ( This is a remote position )
The Donor Officer serves on the GEM US Development team with responsibility for building, cultivating, and stewarding relationships with donors and prospects in order to advance the mission of Greater Europe Mission . The ideal candidate has experience in recruiting, sales, or donor development. They are passionate about building new relationships and working alongside a team that is enthusiastic about the mission field of Europe.
GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES FOR ALL GEM STAFF

• Maintain personal spiritual vitality and a healthy life rhythm.

• Live and work in alignment with GEM’s mission, vision, and core values.

• Participate in required staff meetings, retreats, and organizational gatherings.

• Communicate in a timely, professional, and gracious manner with colleagues, donors, and partners.

• Uphold GEM policies, procedures, and standards of confidentiality and integrity.
SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES
Donor Care & Relationship Management

• Manage an assigned caseload of donors and prospects, focusing on cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

• Conduct regular donor visits and relational touchpoints (in person, phone, and virtual).

• Encourage deeper donor engagement by clearly communicating GEM’s mission, vision, and ministry impact in Europe.

• Identify and help qualify new donor prospects in collaboration with the Development team.
Stewardship & Engagement

• Ensure donors receive timely, thoughtful communication and understand the impact of their generosity.

• Partner with Marketing, field leadership, and missionaries to share stories, updates, and giving opportunities.

• Participate in donor events and gatherings such as Vision Summit, Vision Weekend, and regional or small-group events.

• Maintain accurate donor records, notes, and follow-up in GEM’s CRM.
Team Collaboration

• Work closely with the VP of Development and Development team to support fundraising strategies and goals.

• Contribute to a team-based culture of donor care, accountability, and collaboration.

• Support organizational fundraising initiatives as needed.
TRAVEL
This position requires up to 50% travel. Some of the travel is international.
QUALIFICATIONS
Required

• Clear Christian faith and personal alignment with GEM’s mission and values.

• 3-5 years of relevant experience in development, fundraising, sales, and/or recruiting, with demonstrated strength in relationship-building.

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both written and verbal.

• Ability to manage multiple relationships, priorities, and follow-up effectively.

• Willingness and ability to travel for donor visits and events.
Preferred

• Experience managing a donor portfolio or working in major or mid-level giving.

• Experience in a nonprofit, ministry, or mission-sending organization.

• Familiarity with CRM systems and donor tracking.

title: Contract Writer - A Book For Women Struggling with People-Pleasing
description:
Location: Remote
Position Overview
We are seeking a contract writer to develop and write a Christ-centered book focused on helping women overcome people-pleasing. This project will help women unmask the root causes of approval-seeking behaviors, dismantle the fear of man, and live in the genuine freedom of a heart captivated by the fear of God.
We are open to different conceptual directions for this resource, including:

• A foundational, theological exploration of the "fear of man" vs. the "fear of God." This book would dive deep into theology to uncover how a woman's craving for human approval is ultimately a worship issue. It would offer a robust, gospel-centered framework for understanding our identity in Christ, freeing women from the exhausting, performance-driven cycle of earning love and acceptance.

• A vulnerable, narrative-driven book that uses powerful personal storytelling, memoir-style reflection, and relatable lived experiences to expose the daily, heavy toll of people-pleasing. The author will walk readers through her own struggles with boundary-setting, overcommitment, and the fear of rejection-whether in friendships, marriage, ministry, or family dynamics-while highlighting the liberating grace of Jesus.

The ideal project will combine deep empathy and cultural relevance with rich biblical truth, moving past shallow "assertiveness training" to point women to the ultimate security found in Christ alone.
Scope of Work

• Research, outline, and write a full-length manuscript (approximately 45,000-75,000 words)

• Collaborate closely with the editorial team through multiple rounds of revision

• Ensure theological alignment with The Daily Grace Co. ’s doctrinal commitment

Commitment
Contract, per-project basis.
Compensation
Compensation is determined based on project scope and complexity.
Additional Information
Contractors are engaged based on the needs of specific projects and are not guaranteed ongoing or full-time work. Participation in meetings, workshops, or collaborative sessions may be requested depending on the project timeline.
Why Publish with The Daily Grace Co. ?
With over a decade of publishing experience, The Daily Grace Co. creates Christ-centered resources marked by theological depth, biblical faithfulness, and practical encouragement. We value thoughtful, faithful writers and partner closely from concept development through launch. Our goal is not simply to publish books-but to serve readers with resources that meet real needs and help them treasure Christ.
Proposal Requirements

Important:Proposals that do not include all required components listed below cannot be reviewed.
AI Use:We strongly discourage the use of generative AI in book proposals, and we will not move forward with a book proposal if generative AI is used to generate or refine sample chapters.

Please submit all materials inasingle PDF(not a Word Doc or Google Doc) that includes:
1. Title and Subtitle
2. Controlling Idea (1-2 sentences)
3. One-Paragraph Summary
Provide a concise overview of the book’s purpose, scope, structure, and tone.
4. Target Audience Description (One of the Most Important Sections)Who this book is specifically for

• Their stage or season of life

• The particular struggles, questions, or longings they are experiencing

• Why this book matters to them now

• Tip: Specificity is essential. Broad descriptions such as “Christian women” or “believers” are not sufficient.

5. Comparable Titles (2-3 from the Past 5 Years)
Identify 2-3 comparable books published within the last five years and explain:

• How your book overlaps with each one

• How it is meaningfully distinct in approach, audience, tone, or theological emphasis

6. Author Bio
Explain what uniquely qualifies you to write this book, including:

• Education

• Ministry, counseling, academic, or professional experience

• Subject-matter expertise

• Lived experience relevant to the topic (if appropriate)

• Previous publishing or writing experience
